hints: In right triangle with half-base $8\text{ cm}$ and hypotenuse $10\text{ cm}$, $\cos A = \frac{8}{10} = 0.8 \implies A \approx 0.6435\text{ rad}$.
walkthrough:
In isosceles triangle $\triangle ABC$ ($AC = 16\text{ cm}, AB = BC = 10\text{ cm}$), drop a perpendicular from $B$ to the midpoint of $AC$ (base length $8\text{ cm}$):
$$\cos(\angle BAC) = \frac{8}{10} = 0.8$$
$$\angle BAC = \cos^{-1}(0.8) \approx 0.643501 \approx 0.6435\text{ radians} \quad (\text{to 4 d.p.})$$

ai_rubric.Angle Proof: Shows $\cos A = 0.8$ and concludes $\angle BAC = 0.6435\text{ rad}$ (B1).

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

walkthrough:
Calculate the altitude and area of $\triangle ABC$:
$$h = \sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 6 = 48\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of one circular sector (radius $10\text{ cm}$, angle $0.643501\text{ rad}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector}) = \frac{1}{2}(10^2)(0.643501) = 50 \times 0.643501 = 32.17505\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the central shaded region where the two circular sectors overlap inside $\triangle ABC$:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 2 \times \text{Area}(\text{sector}) - \text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = 2(32.17505) - 48 = 64.3501 - 48 = 16.3501 \approx 16.4\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Overlapping Area: Finds triangle area $48$ (M1, A1). Finds sector area $32.18$ (M1). Computes overlap $2(32.18) - 48 = 16.4\text{ cm}^2$ (M1, A1).
